newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - FTSE options traded in a hedging strategy.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - FTSE options traded in a hedging strategy.

text.p: A certain amount of equity options business on Tuesday concerned closing existing positions for May expiry in stock and index options, dealers said.
Otherwise, the bulk of deals was in the FTSE 100 index options which were busy on mixed trading.
One of the larger deals was a long cylinder in FTSE in which 4,300 June 4775 calls were sold at 40-1/2p and 4,300 June 4600 puts were bought at 37p against buying June FTSE futures at 4707.
This deal is basically bullish -- owing to the long futures position.

But If the market goes above 4775 the position may have to be closed owing to assignment of the short calls. On the other hand, if the market declines and drops below 4600 the losses can contained by exercising the long puts.
By 1440 GMT, spot FTSE was up 19.9 points at 4689.5 while June futures were up 22 at 4706.

Over in stock options a short position was taken in electricals company GEC in which 1,000 August 390 calls were sold at 7p. Dealers believed this was a hedge against the underlying share price falling and was taken by a trader with a holding in the stock. GEC shares added 2-1/2p to 368p.
Elsewhere, in mobile phone company Orange, 800 June 220 calls were bought at 12p by a trader expecting the underlying shares to go up.

And in shipping and transport group Peninsular & Oriental Steam Navigation Co, a bearish position was rolled forward by selling 200 May 650 puts at 31p in a closing deal and buying 200 May 650 calls at 40p.
